findings.title: Trace ID no longer appears in the plugin request completion log
findings.body: logRequest used to add a `traceID` field explicitly via tracing.TraceIDFromContext. That was removed, and the log now relies entirely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to carry it. Nothing in this PR adds trace ID to the contextual attributes (instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). Unless the infra logger's FromContext happens to include the trace ID, completed-request logs silently lose their trace correlation, which is a regression in observability.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded calls
findings.body: FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), so anything logged through the contextual logger is recorded on a throwaway object. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so tests that inject TestLogger and assert on InfoLogs will see zero calls and pass or fail for the wrong reason. The fake should return the receiver (or share its log state) so that calls are observed.

findings.title: No test covers the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the moved logging behavior
findings.body: The contextual logger logic was moved out of the metrics middleware into a new file, and LoggerMiddleware now depends on it for endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname. None of the tests in this PR verify that ContextualLoggerMiddleware adds these attributes to the context, or that LoggerMiddleware's output still includes them. The existing test still only exercises metrics, with the test name still TestInstrumentationMiddleware.

findings.title: Nil request is dereferenced without a guard
findings.body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics read req.PluginContext unconditionally. LoggerMiddleware explicitly guards against a nil req, but this middleware does not. Any caller that passes a nil request into this layer will panic here, which is inconsistent with the rest of the logging chain.
